findings.title: Brand-facing analytics headline/growth/trend can surface a creator-self-declared (unverified) follower count as if Meta-verified
findings.evidence: AnalyticsService.buildMetricsResponse (influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/analytics/AnalyticsService.java:108-199 at RC 115f698) calls creatorMetricsRepository.findByCreatorProfileIdOrderByTimeDesc(authorizedCreatorId, PageRequest.of(0,20)) with NO filter on CreatorMetric.dataSource, then takes latest.get(0) (the single newest row across ALL platforms/sources) as the 'headline' totalFollowers/engagementRate/followerGrowth. PortfolioService.declarePlatform (PortfolioService.java:448-507) lets any authenticated creator write a CreatorMetric row with dataSource=CreatorMetric.DATA_SOURCE_CREATOR_REPORTED and a self-typed followers count up to MAX_SELF_DECLARED_FOLLOWERS=1,000,000,000, with time=Instant.now() — i.e. always newer than any prior Meta-synced row. Because buildMetricsResponse orders by time only, that self-declared row becomes 'mostRecent' and is what AnalyticsController (/analytics/creators/{creatorId}/metrics, brand-facing) and CreatorAnalyticsController (/creator/analytics/me/metrics) return. Confirmed as a real, live defect (not a hypothesis) by the very next commit in this repo's history, e67dc5b9938252f408ad595f5d043f052e25a02a ('fix(analytics): headline, growth and trend read only Meta-synced metric rows (F-0961)'), whose commit message states verbatim: 'AnalyticsService took the newest creator_metrics row of ANY data_source, so a creator-declared (CREATOR_REPORTED) follower count ... became the analytics headline shown to brands.' That commit is NOT an ancestor of 115f698 (git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms 115f698 is an ancestor of e67dc5b, i.e. the fix lands AFTER this RC) — so the RC under audit does not have the fix. AnalyticsServiceTest.java (RC) has 17 green tests (mvn -q -o -Dtest=AnalyticsServiceTest test, exit 0) and contains zero references to dataSource/CREATOR_REPORTED/DATA_SOURCE, confirming the existing suite never exercised this path.
findings.impact: A creator can inflate the follower/engagement/growth numbers a brand sees on the brand-facing analytics pages (/brand/analytics/:creatorId) — and their own self-view — by calling POST /me/portfolio/platforms with a fabricated handle+followers for any self-declarable platform; because the write timestamp is always 'now', it outranks even a fresh Meta poll and becomes the headline shown to brands doing paid/partnership decisions.
findings.recommended_fix: Filter CreatorMetricsRepository reads used for brand/creator analytics headlines to CreatorMetric.DATA_SOURCE_META_API (isPlatformVerified()==true) only, matching the fix already implemented in e67dc5b — add a findByCreatorProfileIdAndDataSourceOrderByTimeDesc finder and apply it (plus the isPlatformVerified in-memory guard) to both the 'latest' lookback and the startDate/endDate trend range in buildMetricsResponse.
findings.verification_required: cd influora-api && mvn -q -o -Dtest=AnalyticsServiceTest test (confirms current green baseline with no dataSource assertions); then add/port the F-0961 test case (25 newer CREATOR_REPORTED rows should not crowd out Meta rows from the 20-row lookback) and confirm it fails on this RC's AnalyticsService before any fix is applied.

findings.title: Public, unauthenticated 'verified metrics' page can display a creator-fabricated follower count under a Meta-verification claim
findings.evidence: PublicCreatorService.getVerifiedMetrics (influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/PublicCreatorService.java:46-103) gates on profile.isDiscoverable() && metaConnected (an active, non-expired, non-revoked meta_oauth_tokens row) && !profile.isSuspended(), then reads creatorMetricsRepository.findByCreatorProfileIdOrderByTimeDesc(profile.getId(), PageRequest.of(0,1)).stream().findFirst() — the single newest CreatorMetric row for the creator, with NO filter on dataSource and NO filter on platform. The method's own comment says "the metric row IS the platform-API evidence behind this snapshot" and the frontend page this serves (/c/:username/verified) is explicitly the 'verified-metrics' surface (class javadoc: T-MEERA-CREATOR-PHASE-A). Because PortfolioService.declarePlatform (see BLUEPRINT-01) lets a Meta-connected creator ALSO self-declare a different platform (e.g. YouTube/TikTok/Twitter — SELF_DECLARABLE_PLATFORMS) with a followers value up to 1,000,000,000 and a fresh timestamp, that self-declared row — never Meta-verified, PlatformStat.verified stays false for it — becomes 'latest' here too and is served, unauthenticated, on a page whose whole purpose is to prove Meta-verified numbers to any visiting brand or the public. Unlike AnalyticsService, this file/service was untouched by the F-0961 fix commit (e67dc5b touches only AnalyticsService.java + CreatorMetricsRepository.java + one new repository test, per `git show --stat e67dc5b`), so this exposure is not even addressed by that later fix. PublicCreatorServiceTest.java (RC) has 4 green tests (mvn -q -o -Dtest=PublicCreatorServiceTest test, exit 0) with zero references to dataSource/CREATOR_REPORTED.
findings.impact: A logged-in creator can make their own PUBLIC, unauthenticated 'verified' profile page (/c/:username/verified) — which explicitly claims to be Meta-API-sourced evidence — display an arbitrary, self-typed follower count up to 1 billion, with no visual distinction from real Meta data, to any brand or member of the public who visits the link. This is a direct follower-fraud / fake-verification vector on the one page in the product whose entire purpose is fraud-resistant verification.
findings.recommended_fix: Apply the same DATA_SOURCE_META_API / isPlatformVerified() filter used for BLUEPRINT-01's fix to PublicCreatorService.getVerifiedMetrics's CreatorMetric lookup, and additionally scope it to the platform the creator's active meta_oauth_tokens row actually represents (currently platform-agnostic too).
findings.verification_required: Write/port a PublicCreatorServiceTest case: creator has an active Meta connection + one old META_API CreatorMetric row + one newer CREATOR_REPORTED row for a different platform; assert getVerifiedMetrics returns the META_API row's followers, not the newer declared one. Expect it to fail on this RC.

findings.title: PortfolioController has no controller-level test — only service-level unit tests across 6 files
findings.evidence: find influora-api/src/test for *PortfolioController* returns zero results; find for *PortfolioService* returns 6 files (PortfolioServiceTest, PortfolioServiceContactTest, PortfolioServiceDeclarePlatformTest, PortfolioServicePublicVisibilityTest, PortfolioServiceRateCardTest, PortfolioServiceCollabDisplayModeTest). None of the 7 REST endpoints on PortfolioController (GET/PATCH /me/portfolio, GET /portfolio/{username}, POST /portfolio/{username}/contact, POST /me/portfolio/sync, POST /me/portfolio/platforms, POST /me/portfolio/cover, GET /me/portfolio/analytics) has a MockMvc/@WebMvcTest exercising request binding, validation annotations (@Valid on PortfolioPatchRequest/PortfolioContactRequest), multipart handling for the cover upload, or the actual HTTP status/JSON envelope contract — all of that is inferred, never executed.
findings.impact: A regression in request binding (e.g. a renamed/retyped field on PortfolioPatchRequest, a wrong @RequestPart name on the cover upload, a validation annotation silently dropped) would not be caught by any existing automated test in this RC, even though the underlying service logic is well covered.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a PortfolioControllerTest (@WebMvcTest(PortfolioController.class)) covering each endpoint's request/response contract and validation errors, mirroring the pattern used for AnalyticsControllerTest/MetaOAuthControllerTest which do exist.
findings.verification_required: Confirm absence is not a tooling artifact: `find influora-api/src/test -iname '*PortfolioController*'` from the RC root.

findings.title: PortfolioAnalyticsResponse.linkClicks is permanently an empty list — custom-link click tracking was never implemented
findings.evidence: PortfolioService.analytics() (PortfolioService.java:596-639) returns `List.of()` for the linkClicks field with the inline comment 'Link clicks require custom link tracking (not implemented)'. profileClicks is also explicitly a proxy estimate (totalFollowers/100) flagged profileClicksEstimated=true, not a real click count.
findings.impact: The creator-facing Portfolio Analytics panel (GET /me/portfolio/analytics) can never show real per-link click data; any UI element built to render PortfolioAnalyticsResponse.linkClicks with real numbers is dead by construction until a link-tracking event/table is added.
findings.recommended_fix: Either implement per-custom-link click tracking (a portfolio_events row per link click keyed by link id) or remove/hide the linkClicks affordance from the FE until it is real, to avoid an honest-but-always-empty UI element reading as broken.
findings.verification_required: None beyond the code read — this is an openly documented gap, not a hidden defect.

findings.title: CreatorOnboardingController POST /onboarding/creator/socials is a permanently dead endpoint by design (CR-108)
findings.evidence: CreatorOnboardingService.connectSocial (CreatorOnboardingService.java:80-88) unconditionally throws ApiException SOCIAL_OAUTH_NOT_IMPLEMENTED / 501 for every platform including INSTAGRAM, per its own javadoc (CR-108): Instagram now has a real dedicated flow via MetaOAuthController and 'the frontend never calls this endpoint any more'. Confirmed by CreatorOnboardingServiceTest#testConnectSocialRefusesFabricatedConnectionForUnimplementedPlatform and #testConnectSocialRefusesInstagramToo (both green, asserting exactly this 501 for YOUTUBE and INSTAGRAM).
findings.impact: None in practice — this is an intentional, tested, honest refusal rather than a fabricated success, and the frontend (creator-onboarding.tsx) shows a 'coming soon' toast locally instead of calling this route. Recorded here only because the feature list names this endpoint explicitly; its correct classification is INCOMPLETE-BY-DESIGN, not broken.
findings.recommended_fix: None required for correctness. If/when real YouTube/TikTok/Twitter OAuth (CR-119) ships, this refusal should be narrowed per-platform rather than removed wholesale.
findings.verification_required: cd influora-api && mvn -q -o -Dtest=CreatorOnboardingServiceTest test (green, 15 tests, confirms this behavior).

findings.title: CreatorConnectNudgeJob is disabled by default and has no operator-facing send-count/failure metric beyond logs
findings.evidence: application.yml:321-322: `creator-connect-nudge: enabled: ${CREATOR_CONNECT_NUDGE_ENABLED:false}` — confirmed default false. CreatorConnectNudgeJob.sendNudges() (CreatorConnectNudgeJob.java:86-96) returns immediately when !enabled. The job's own javadoc states this is deliberate ('mails real people on a schedule'). No test file under influora-api/src/test named *CreatorConnectNudgeJob* was located in this pass (not exhaustively confirmed) so whether the 3-stage delay sequencing is test-covered is unverified within budget.
findings.impact: Matches the task's stated expectation (flag default false) — this is confirmation, not a new defect. Included because production go-live sign-off should explicitly confirm CREATOR_CONNECT_NUDGE_ENABLED is left false (or deliberately flipped) rather than assuming.
findings.recommended_fix: No code fix needed; an ops checklist item to confirm the env var's intended value in each deploy target.
findings.verification_required: grep CREATOR_CONNECT_NUDGE_ENABLED in the actual deploy env files/secrets (out of scope for a source-only audit).

features.name: Meta OAuth authorize/callback/status/disconnect
features.purpose: Creator-initiated Instagram/Facebook OAuth connect: mint state, redirect to Meta, exchange code for a long-lived token scoped to the creator (never a workspace), resolve IG business account + granted scopes, report status, and disconnect.
features.entry_point: src/lib/api.ts metaOAuth.authorize/handleCallback/getStatus/disconnect -> MetaOAuthController.java:65-189 (GET /meta/oauth/authorize|callback|status, POST /meta/oauth/disconnect); FE redirect target src/pages (callback route consumes MetaCallbackResponse)
features.flow: FE Settings page -> api.ts GET /meta/oauth/authorize -> MetaOAuthController.authorize -> MetaOAuthStateStore.issue + MetaOAuthService.build*AuthorizationUrl -> browser navigates to Meta -> Meta redirects to FE callback route with code/state -> api.ts GET /meta/oauth/callback -> MetaOAuthController.callback -> MetaOAuthStateStore.consumePath -> CreatorProfileRepository.findByUserId -> CreatorMetaOAuthService.connect(creatorProfileId, code, authPath) -> MetaOAuthService.exchangeCodeForToken/exchangeForLongLivedToken (or Instagram-Login equivalents) -> FacebookPageClient.resolveConnectedInstagram / fetchPermissions -> MetaGraphApiClient (GET /me?fields=id) -> MetaTokenStorage.storeCreatorToken (meta_oauth_tokens, workspace_id NULL) -> ApplicationEventPublisher publishes CreatorMetaConnectedEvent (kicks async caption sync) -> ApiResponse<MetaCallbackResponse>
features.database: meta_oauth_tokens (creator_profile_id, workspace_id NULLABLE, access_token encrypted, expires_at, granted_scopes, ig_business_account_id, meta_user_id, auth_path, revoked, instagram_username)
features.state_machine: not-connected -> (authorize+callback) -> connected(business, connected=true) | connected(personal, connected=false, token still stored) -> (disconnect | Meta deauthorize/data-deletion callback) -> revoked
features.authn: requireCreator(principal) — CREATOR UserType only, 403 WRONG_USER_TYPE otherwise; JWT required (no permitAll on any of these 4 routes)
features.authz: requireCreatorProfile resolves creatorProfileId ONLY from principal.getUserId() -> CreatorProfileRepository.findByUserId — a caller can never supply another creator's id (IDOR-safe by construction per the controller's own javadoc, and consistent with what the code does)
features.working_condition: authorize correctly refuses (503, typed codes) when either Meta app pair is unconfigured or the redirect-URI is unusable, verified per in-code comments as 'live 2026-08-28' and 'live 2026-09-12' regressions now fixed; callback correctly resolves state->authPath, never trusts a client-supplied path; connect() stores tokens creator-scoped (nullable workspace_id) fixing a previously-fatal NOT NULL violation; CR-114 default ~60-day expiry fallback prevents a 0-second-lifetime token on a missing expires_in; CR-104 grantedScopes is the real /me/permissions result, not the requested set.
features.failure_conditions: META_INSTAGRAM_LOGIN_NOT_CONFIGURED/META_NOT_CONFIGURED/503 pre-flight refusals; META_OAUTH_STATE_INVALID/400 on expired/reused/forged state; INSTAGRAM_ACCOUNT_NOT_PROFESSIONAL/400 (F-0891) when Instagram account-type probe positively identifies a personal account (fails OPEN on probe failure or unrecognized type, by design); CREATOR_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND/404; graph API resolution failures (IG account, permissions, /me id) are individually swallowed (logged, null-returned) so a transient Graph failure never fails a connect whose token exchange already succeeded.
features.security_conditions: Token stored encrypted (MetaTokenStorage, not opened in this pass) scoped to creator only (workspace_id NULL), never mixed with workspace-scoped rows per the controller's documented prior bug (a CREATOR principal has no workspaceId — a pre-fix insert with null workspace against a NOT NULL column always failed; fixed by V20260721150000 making it nullable). State token is CSRF-bound and single-use (consumePath).
features.tests: MetaOAuthControllerTest.java, MetaOAuthServiceTest.java, MetaOAuthServiceInstagramDiagnosticsTest.java, MetaOAuthServiceUriEncodingTest.java, CreatorMetaOAuthServiceTest.java, CreatorMetaOAuthServiceInstagramLoginTest.java, MetaConnectionServiceTest.java, MetaOAuthTokenRepositoryMetaUserIdTest.java, MetaOAuthTokenRepositoryNullWorkspaceIdTest.java all present (9 test files); none independently re-run in this pass beyond confirming their existence and reading CreatorMetaOAuthService's own extensive in-code documentation of past live bugs and their fixes.
features.production_conditions: META_APP_ID/META_APP_SECRET (Facebook pair) and/or META_INSTAGRAM_APP_ID/SECRET (Instagram-Login pair) must be configured per MetaApiProperties; redirect-URI must resolve to a public FE route, not this API path (a previously-live bug, fixed, per authorize()'s own comment).
features.validation: authPath enum-typed (MetaAuthPath), defaults to FACEBOOK_LOGIN; code/state required non-blank via Spring's @RequestParam.
known_issues: This pass did not independently execute the 9 existing test files (relied on their presence + the source's own extensive documented-bug/fix trail) — recommend a targeted mvn run of MetaOAuthControllerTest + CreatorMetaOAuthServiceTest before go-live sign-off to convert this from IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED to VERIFIED WORKING.

features.name: Meta deauthorize + data-deletion callbacks (permitAll)
features.purpose: Meta App Review-required webhooks: when a user removes the app from Instagram/Facebook settings (deauthorize) or requests data deletion, Meta POSTs a signed_request here so Influora can stop polling and record the request for the manual 30-day deletion process.
features.entry_point: Meta platform (server-to-server, no FE involved) -> MetaPlatformCallbackController.java:137,206 (POST /webhooks/meta/deauthorize, POST /webhooks/meta/data-deletion)
features.flow: Meta -> POST /webhooks/meta/{deauthorize,data-deletion} (form-urlencoded signed_request) -> verifyOrReject -> verify() [base64url split, HMAC-SHA256 over BOTH configured app secrets (Facebook and Instagram-Login), algorithm-confusion guard checked AFTER the HMAC, constant-time compare] -> runOncePerDelivery (IdempotencyService keyed on kind+userRef-hash+issued_at) -> MetaTokenStorage.revokeByMetaUserId -> AuditLogService.recordToolCall (audit_log, no PII, only a truncated SHA-256 userRef) -> 200 empty body (deauthorize) or JSON {url, confirmation_code} (data-deletion)
features.api: POST /webhooks/meta/deauthorize (200, empty body); POST /webhooks/meta/data-deletion (200, DataDeletionResponse {url, confirmation_code})
features.database: meta_oauth_tokens (revoked flag, via revokeByMetaUserId keyed on meta_user_id for FACEBOOK_LOGIN rows or ig_business_account_id for INSTAGRAM_LOGIN rows); audit_log (append-only record of the callback, no raw Meta user id)
features.state_machine: connected -> (verified deauthorize OR data-deletion callback) -> revoked (idempotent no-op on replay of the same issued_at)
features.authn: None — SecurityConfig explicitly permitAll for exactly these two POST paths (not a wildcard /webhooks/meta/**, per the controller's own comment 'so a future Meta endpoint cannot inherit permitAll by accident'), confirmed by direct grep of SecurityConfig.java:133-137
features.authz: Trust boundary is the HMAC signature, not a session — verified BEFORE any payload field is parsed/trusted; tries both configured app secrets so either the Facebook or Instagram-Login app can be the signer, fails closed on a blank/unconfigured secret
features.working_condition: A request with a valid signed_request from either configured app matches, revokes the matching (non-revoked) token row if one is found, and always returns Meta's expected 2xx; every failure mode (absent param, malformed shape, no configured secret, wrong algorithm, bad signature, missing user_id) collapses to the SAME generic 400, preventing the endpoint being used as an app-configuration or user-existence oracle.
features.failure_conditions: INVALID_SIGNED_REQUEST/400 for any verification failure (deliberately generic); a verified callback that matches no non-revoked token row (revoked==0) is NOT an error to Meta (still 200, avoiding an endless Meta retry loop) but is logged as an operational anomaly requiring manual follow-up.
features.security_conditions: Exactly the algorithm-confusion, constant-time-compare, verify-before-parse, and fail-closed-on-blank-secret disciplines the class javadoc claims are mirrored from WebhookSignatureVerifier/RazorpayWebhookController; the raw Meta user id never reaches a log line or audit record (only its truncated SHA-256).
features.tests: MetaPlatformCallbackControllerTest.java exists (present, ~confirmed via file listing) with a matching surefire report on disk (target/surefire-reports/...MetaPlatformCallbackControllerTest.txt/.xml) proving it has been run at least once in this workspace's build history; not independently re-run fresh in this pass.
features.production_conditions: Requires influora.web-base-url configured (used to build the data-deletion status URL to /meta-data-policy); requires at least one of the two Meta app secret pairs configured for any callback to verify at all.
features.monitoring: log.warn on a verified-but-unmatched deauthorize/deletion (revoked==0) — surfaced only via application logs in this pass, no dedicated alert wiring observed/traced.
features.validation: Exactly-two-segment signed_request format check (rejects a 3-segment token), base64url decode guard, non-empty signature/payload guard, JSON-object guard, required algorithm literal HMAC-SHA256, required non-blank user_id.
known_issues: Class javadoc records that C5 (resolveMetaUserIdSafely) is a best-effort Graph call that can return null on transient failure, meaning a pre-C5-migration token row (or one where that resolution failed at connect time) may never be matched by a later deauthorize/deletion callback — expected/documented behavior, not independently re-verified in this pass.

features.name: Creator analytics brand-view + self-view

features.entry_point: src/lib/api.ts creatorMetrics/creatorScores/creatorDemographics/contentPerformance (brand) and the creator/analytics/me/* equivalents -> AnalyticsController.java:61-106 (GET /analytics/creators/{creatorId}/metrics|scores|demographics|media) and CreatorAnalyticsController.java:37-70 (GET /creator/analytics/me/metrics|scores|demographics|media)

AnalyticsService.buildMetricsResponse labels mostRecent.getAvgReachPerPost() as 'totalReach' in the response even though the underlying field is a per-post average, not a sum — a naming/semantics mismatch worth confirming against the FE's rendering of that field (not independently traced to the FE component in this pass).

features.name: Portfolio public/contact + own get/patch/sync/platforms/cover/analytics
features.purpose: Public portfolio page + contact form; creator's own portfolio CRUD, Meta-backed sync, no-Meta platform self-declaration, cover image upload, and portfolio analytics (page views/inquiries/media-kit downloads).
features.entry_point: src/pages creator-portfolio-editor.tsx / creator-portfolio-public.tsx -> src/lib/api.ts portfolio.* -> PortfolioController.java:40-105 (GET/PATCH /me/portfolio, GET /portfolio/{username}, POST /portfolio/{username}/contact, POST /me/portfolio/{sync,platforms,cover}, GET /me/portfolio/analytics)
features.flow: Public: FE creator-portfolio-public.tsx -> api.ts GET /portfolio/{username} -> PortfolioController.getPublic -> PortfolioService.getPublic (assemble page: profile, collabs, rate card, badges, top audience cities) -> PortfolioService.recordPublicView (own @Transactional call, exceptions swallowed in the controller so a view-counter failure never 500s the page). Contact: POST /portfolio/{username}/contact -> requireDiscoverablePortfolio -> field validation -> AbuseThrottleService (20/hr per creator, keyed by profile id not sender IP) -> PortfolioContactEvent published on the event bus (W3-1 fix: previously constructed but never published) -> NotificationService (async). Own: PATCH/GET /me/portfolio, POST /me/portfolio/sync (Meta-backed, writes a META_API CreatorMetric + upserts PlatformStat), POST /me/portfolio/platforms (declarePlatform, writes a CREATOR_REPORTED CreatorMetric, refuses if the platform is already Meta-verified), POST /me/portfolio/cover (magic-byte MIME sniff, malware scan, stream-to-R2, presigned GET on read), GET /me/portfolio/analytics (real page views + delta from portfolio_events, real media-kit-download count, an explicitly-labeled ESTIMATED profileClicks proxy, and an always-empty linkClicks list).
features.api: GET /portfolio/{username} (permitAll); POST /portfolio/{username}/contact (permitAll); GET/PATCH /me/portfolio; POST /me/portfolio/sync; POST /me/portfolio/platforms; POST /me/portfolio/cover (multipart); GET /me/portfolio/analytics
features.database: creator_profiles, platform_stats, creator_metrics, portfolio_events, collaborations, deliverables, reviews, workspaces, audience_demographics, meta_oauth_tokens
features.state_machine: PlatformStat.verified: false (declarePlatform, CREATOR_REPORTED) vs true (syncPlatforms, META_API) — declarePlatform explicitly refuses (PLATFORM_ALREADY_VERIFIED/409) to overwrite an already-verified row, keeping that specific table honest even though the CreatorMetric-level analytics read (BLUEPRINT-01/02) does not consult PlatformStat.verified at all.
features.authn: Public routes (GET /portfolio/{username}, POST .../contact) are permitAll per SecurityConfig.java:183-186 (confirmed by grep); all /me/portfolio/** routes require a creator JWT.
features.authz: requireDiscoverablePortfolio gates the public GET/contact routes on profile.isDiscoverable(); /me/portfolio/** routes resolve the profile only via CreatorContextService.requireCreatorProfile(principal), never a client-supplied id.
features.working_condition: getPublic/getMine/updateMine/uploadCover/contact/analytics all have dedicated PortfolioService*Test coverage (6 files: PortfolioServiceTest, ...ContactTest, ...DeclarePlatformTest, ...PublicVisibilityTest, ...RateCardTest, ...CollabDisplayModeTest); declarePlatform correctly refuses to downgrade an already-verified PlatformStat row and correctly labels its own row as unverified at the PlatformStat level — but see BLUEPRINT-01/02 for the analytics-read-side gap that undermines this at the CreatorMetric level.
features.failure_conditions: NOT_CONNECTED/409 (no active Meta token, or token row missing ig_business_account_id) and TOKEN_EXPIRED/409 for sync; INVALID_PLATFORM/INVALID_HANDLE/INVALID_FOLLOWERS/400 and PLATFORM_ALREADY_VERIFIED/409 for declarePlatform; INVALID_FILE/STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE/FILE_TOO_LARGE/400-503 for cover upload; TOO_MANY_REQUESTS/429 for contact past the per-creator hourly cap.
features.security_conditions: Contact throttle keyed by RECIPIENT creator (not sender IP) so a distributed attacker can't route around it by rotating IPs, layered on top of an edge per-IP filter (AuthRateLimitFilter). Sender email/PII is explicitly NOT logged (T-FESTIVALBOX-0905 fix noted in-code). Cover upload does magic-byte MIME sniffing + malware scan before ever streaming to R2, and persists only the object key (never a public URL) — reads go through a time-limited presigned GET.
features.tests: 6 PortfolioService*Test files present and (per file listing) exercise contact/declarePlatform/public-visibility/rate-card/collab-display-mode paths; PortfolioControllerTest is ABSENT (see BLUEPRINT-03) — controller-level request binding/validation is not independently verified.
features.production_conditions: R2 (cover upload) must be configured; AbuseThrottleService backing store (likely Redis/DB, not traced) must be reachable for the contact throttle to function at all — if it fails, this pass did not trace whether the code fails open or closed.
features.monitoring: log.warn on a failed public-view record (swallowed, never surfaces to the caller) and on throttled contact attempts.
features.performance: ANALYTICS_WINDOW=30 days fixed; CONTACT_THROTTLE_WINDOW=1 hour / MAX_CONTACT_PER_CREATOR_PER_WINDOW=20 fixed constants, not configurable.
features.validation: @Valid on PortfolioPatchRequest/PortfolioContactRequest; declarePlatform validates platform enum membership, handle regex (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,60}$), and follower bounds (0..1e9) inline (not via @Valid).
known_issues: BLUEPRINT-04: PortfolioAnalyticsResponse.linkClicks is permanently List.of() — link-click tracking was never built.

declarePlatform's own honesty guarantees (PlatformStat.verified stays false) are undermined at the analytics-read layer by BLUEPRINT-01/02 — the CreatorMetric row it writes is exactly the row that can leak into the brand-facing/public 'verified' surfaces.

features.name: Creator profile GET/PATCH /me/creator-profile + public verified metrics
features.purpose: Creator's own profile self-view/edit (MeCreatorProfileController) and a public, unauthenticated, cache-disabled 'verified metrics' snapshot page for Meta-connected, discoverable, non-suspended creators (PublicCreatorController).
features.entry_point: src/pages creator-profile.tsx -> api.ts GET/PATCH /me/creator-profile -> MeCreatorProfileController.java (whole file); src/pages c/:username/verified -> api.ts -> PublicCreatorController.java:36-55 (GET /public/creators/{username}/verified)
features.flow: Self: FE -> api.ts -> MeCreatorProfileController.get/patch -> CreatorProfileService.getMyProfile/patchMyProfile (not independently opened in this pass) -> creator_profiles/users tables. Public: FE /c/:username/verified -> api.ts -> PublicCreatorController.getVerifiedMetrics -> feature-flag check (MeeraCreatorFeatureProperties.isCreatorEnabled(), checked BEFORE any DB touch) -> PublicCreatorService.getVerifiedMetrics -> CreatorProfileRepository.findByUsernameIgnoreCase -> gate on isDiscoverable && an active-non-expired-non-revoked MetaOAuthToken && !isSuspended (all three folded into the SAME 404 CREATOR_NOT_FOUND, a documented non-enumeration property) -> CreatorMetricsRepository.findByCreatorProfileIdOrderByTimeDesc(...,1) [UNFILTERED by dataSource — see BLUEPRINT-02] -> CollaborationRepository completed-deal count -> VerifiedProfileResponse, served with Cache-Control: no-store, private (explicitly to defeat an intermediary CDN/proxy cache continuing to serve a stale snapshot after opt-out/suspension).
features.database: creator_profiles, users (self path); creator_profiles, creator_metrics, meta_oauth_tokens, collaborations (public verified path)
features.state_machine: Public verified page: served (200) only when discoverable && metaConnected && !suspended, else uniformly 404 — 3 independent 'hide' conditions collapsed into one response so none can be distinguished by an external caller.
features.authn: GET/PATCH /me/creator-profile require a creator JWT; GET /public/creators/{username}/verified is fully unauthenticated (permitAll, confirmed by the controller's own javadoc referencing an explicit SecurityConfig entry for this exact route).
features.authz: Self routes scoped to the authenticated principal only (not independently re-opened for CreatorProfileService in this pass). Public route has no authz concept by design — it is a public page; its only gates are the 3 folded-into-404 conditions above.
features.working_condition: PublicCreatorService correctly folds 'never existed' / 'not discoverable' / 'token expired (not just revoked)' / 'suspended' into the identical 404 — 2 explicitly documented fixes (Priya Q6: expiry, not just revocation; Priya Q10: suspension was never checked before) are present and confirmed by reading the code; the feature flag is checked before any DB call. HOWEVER the metrics snapshot itself is subject to BLUEPRINT-02 — the single most-recent CreatorMetric row is served with no dataSource or platform filter, so a self-declared (CREATOR_REPORTED) number can be shown on this explicitly 'verified' public page.
features.failure_conditions: FEATURE_DISABLED/404 when MeeraCreatorFeatureProperties.isCreatorEnabled()==false; CREATOR_NOT_FOUND/404 for any of the 3 folded gate conditions above.
features.security_conditions: PublicCreatorService's own javadoc states it is 'deliberately narrow: NO rates, NO floors ... NO PAN/GSTIN/tax identity' — confirmed by the VerifiedProfileResponse shape read in this pass (username, displayName, city, categories, metrics, completedDeals, generatedAt only). Cache-Control: no-store defeats stale-cache replay of an opted-out/suspended creator's data — a documented, verified fix (Priya gate review round 1, Q10).
features.tests: PublicCreatorServiceTest.java (4 tests, confirmed GREEN in this pass via `mvn -q -o -Dtest=PublicCreatorServiceTest test`, exit 0; zero references to dataSource/CREATOR_REPORTED confirmed by grep — the direct coverage-gap evidence for BLUEPRINT-02); PublicCreatorControllerTest.java and MeCreatorProfileControllerTest.java / CreatorProfileServiceTest.java present but not independently re-run in this pass.
features.production_conditions: MeeraCreatorFeatureProperties.isCreatorEnabled() must be true in the target environment for this route to serve anything but 404 — a rollback flag, per the controller's own comment.
features.performance: Single most-recent-row query (PageRequest.of(0,1)) — cheap, but see BLUEPRINT-02 for the correctness issue with that query's lack of filtering.
features.validation: Path variable only (username); no request body on either public route.
known_issues: BLUEPRINT-02 (P0): the public 'verified' page can display a creator-fabricated, non-Meta-verified follower count under an explicit Meta-verification claim — this is the single highest-severity finding in this feature set because the page is public, unauthenticated, and its entire purpose is fraud-resistant verification.
required_fixes: Filter PublicCreatorService.getVerifiedMetrics's CreatorMetric lookup to DATA_SOURCE_META_API / isPlatformVerified()==true, and ideally to the specific platform the active meta_oauth_tokens row represents.

features.name: Background jobs: MetricsPollingJob, AudienceDemographicsJob, MetaTokenRefreshService, PlatformStatsAggregationJob, CreatorConnectNudgeJob
features.user_type: system (scheduled, no direct end-user entry point)
features.purpose: Keep creator_metrics/audience_demographics/platform_stats fresh from Meta on a schedule, refresh expiring tokens ahead of use, and (when explicitly enabled) email creators who registered but never connected Meta.
features.entry_point: Spring @Scheduled cron triggers (no HTTP entry point) — influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/job/{MetricsPollingJob,AudienceDemographicsJob,MetaTokenRefreshService,PlatformStatsAggregationJob,CreatorConnectNudgeJob}.java
features.flow: Each job independently queries its relevant repository for eligible creators/tokens, calls Meta Graph (via MetaGraphApiClient/InstagramInsightsClient/FacebookPageClient, not independently traced per-job in this pass beyond MetricsPollingJob's class javadoc reference), and writes CreatorMetric/AudienceDemographics/PlatformStat rows or refreshes meta_oauth_tokens.access_token/expires_at. CreatorConnectNudgeJob instead anti-joins meta_oauth_tokens to find never-connected creators and publishes CreatorNotConnectedEvent (3-stage, outbox-deduped by idempotency_key, never purged).
features.api: None (no HTTP surface) — confirmed schedules: MetricsPollingJob `0 0 */6 * * *` UTC (every 6h); AudienceDemographicsJob `0 30 3 * * SUN` UTC (weekly); MetaTokenRefreshService `0 30 2 * * *` UTC (nightly); PlatformStatsAggregationJob `0 45 3 * * *` UTC (nightly); CreatorConnectNudgeJob `${influora.creator-connect-nudge.cron:0 30 9 * * *}` Asia/Kolkata (daily, IF enabled).
features.database: creator_metrics, audience_demographics, platform_stats, meta_oauth_tokens, email_outbox (CreatorConnectNudgeJob, keyed by idempotency_key = eventType:entityId:userId, entityId carrying the nudge stage)
features.state_machine: CreatorConnectNudgeJob: unconnected-day-0 -> (day>=1) stage1 sent -> (day>=4) stage2 sent -> (day>=10) stage3 sent -> permanently silent thereafter, OR exits the eligible set entirely the moment any meta_oauth_tokens row (even soft-revoked) exists for that creator, per its own documented anti-join semantics.
features.authn: N/A — server-internal scheduled jobs, no caller identity.
features.working_condition: Confirmed via source+config only in this pass: all 5 jobs exist with the exact cron expressions the task's pointers describe, and CreatorConnectNudgeJob's `enabled` flag defaults to false both in the @Value default (CreatorConnectNudgeJob.java:70) and in application.yml (CREATOR_CONNECT_NUDGE_ENABLED:false) — 2 independent confirmations of the same fact. Actual runtime behavior (does a 6-hourly poll really complete inside its window, does MetaTokenRefreshService actually prevent expiry-related sync failures) was NOT executed or independently traced method-by-method in this pass — budget was spent verifying the analytics-read defect (BLUEPRINT-01/02) instead, which sits directly downstream of what these jobs write.
features.failure_conditions: Not independently traced in this pass beyond MetricsPollingJob's own javadoc noting its on-demand-sync companion 'never throws — a failure here must not surface anywhere; the creator simply waits for the next cron run'.
features.security_conditions: Not independently traced in this pass.
features.tests: Not enumerated/opened in this pass beyond confirming the 5 job source files exist and reading their @Scheduled annotations; job-specific test files were not searched for within this pass's budget.
features.production_conditions: Depends on the same Meta app credentials as the OAuth flow; ShedLock (`@SchedulerLock`, seen on CreatorConnectNudgeJob) implies a distributed lock store is required in a multi-instance deployment for at-most-once execution — not independently confirmed for the other 4 jobs in this pass.
known_issues: This feature entry has the lowest evidence depth of the 7 in this blueprint — only cron/flag configuration was confirmed; per-job internal logic (batching, Graph error handling, partial-failure semantics) was read for MetricsPollingJob's class-level javadoc only and not for the other 4 jobs, due to this pass's time budget. Recommend a follow-up pass reading each job's full method body plus its test file before treating any of the 5 as VERIFIED WORKING.
required_fixes: Follow-up: independently open and (where a test exists) execute AudienceDemographicsJobTest / MetaTokenRefreshServiceTest / PlatformStatsAggregationJobTest / MetricsPollingJobTest / CreatorConnectNudgeJobTest (file names not yet confirmed to exist) to raise this feature's evidence score above 2.
